watchlist.notes: If prices fall too far from the intrinsic value estimated at around 40+ (33 with margin of safety). Toll road like business, not affected by oil pricesd but affected by the flow. Moat is real, hard to replicate the network, although it is a capital hungry business and takes in lots of debt to sustain growth. Also retains more than half to fuel growth but OEs has been growing steadily over the years. Key risk would be recession / significant reduced usage of the gas pipeline

ideas.title: Refinery MRO
ideas.body:
1. Several transcripts from MRO companies state that they anticipate lower MRO requirements for rest of 2026 and higher in 2027 due to the geopolitical tensions - refiners cannot afford to shutdown plants 
2. Likely more extension MRO required when they do eventually shut down plants for MRO - could be when fuel prices come down / when geopolitcal tensions ease

APTV.text:
1. Intrinsic value should be closer to US$70/sh. 
2. Likely to do well if market shifts focus to Physcial AI since many of the parts that they are supplying to EV makers right now would be relevant for Physcial AI
3. More capital-light post-spinoff; allow for higher capital return to shareholders should there be more favourable investment opportunities - at US$39/sh downside is likely limited

ADBE.text:
1. GenAI is not going to replace ADBE. Labs are deprioritizing image and video genAI due to high compute requirements - if we are truly compute constrained then tokens will be allocated to the highest ROI use case which is language token which can do productive work.
2. Will still be cheaper to do via conventional tools that ADBE offer. If Canva and Figma can truly disrupt ADBE, it would've done so long ago but company's Owners' Earnings has been growing steadily over past decade i.e. true franchise that will be hard to disrupt
3. Cash cow - high share repurchase. Trading at 10x Owners' Earnings. Low capital requirements mean it will do well in inflationary environment and high cash flow will make it a good candidate in high yield environment

DECK.text:
1. Company seems well managed, price seems very reasonable. High margins, committed 80% of FCF to buyback
2. However, too hard to determine longevity of moat - trends in footwear can be hard to predict and extremely cyclical. A lot of the apparel brands' share price are down (which could indicate peak pessimism though)
3. Well managed company that is very capital efficient. 
4. Thesis could be that the Hoka brand is not the trendy brand, never has been. Known more for quality - which I think is a more durable moat than fashion trends, which can change quickly. And that company has been compounding since a decade ago and has seen many trends come and go. 
5. Broader apparel / shoewear industry is down, could be indiscriminate selldown here

SHOE.text:
1. Market cap of US$380m, cash and cash equivalent of about US$135m. Essentially US$245m for their operating business 
2. Owners' earnings should be around US$30-40m for this coming year (~US$50m for the latest fiscal year). i.e. about 7x P/OE
3. They are also planning to close around 18-24 stores over the next 2 years, which should release around 15-20m of working capital. If OE can sustain at around 30-40m with this minimised footprint, then P/OE should be around 4x if share price drops to $11 - reasonable entry

ARM.text:
1) Agentic Workflows will require significantly  more CPU. CPUs are increasingly run on ARM architecture (alternative being x86) due to higher efficiency 
2) Corroborated across earnings call by BABA and NVDA which see agentic workflow taking off - also evidenced by Meta's Muse agent and Grokbot, which run on their own VM

LDOS.text:
LDOS (Leidos) - NOTES
Dated 2026-11-10 | Source: OE pipeline run 2026-11-06, Q3 FY26 10-Q, Q3 call

THESIS
- Owner earnings (OE) are strong, and the bear case still holds up. Fair entry is $115-120, but it is a tactical hold, not a long-term compounder.

NUMBERS (OE pipeline, run 6 Nov)
- Anchor OE $1,471m. FY26 OE $1,519m. Price at valuation $135.40.
- Value per share: bear $152.5 (0% growth), base $197.1 (5%), bull $230 (8%). Discounted at 10%.
- Pipeline "buy below" is $118.9, so $115-120 sits right on it. The entry is about 12-15% below the current price.
- Capital light: capex is under 1% of revenue, and OE is about 100% of net income.

WHY IT HOLDS UP
- Backlog is $49.6bn (about 2.7 years of revenue). Funded backlog is $11.1bn, up 22%.
- Free cash flow is about $1.5bn for the nine months. Buybacks have cut shares by about 3.5%.
- Defense and Homeland are growing, and Q3 profit outside Health was strong.

WHY NOT A LONG-TERM HOLD
- About 49% of revenue comes from one customer group, and nearly all the rest from the wider US government. The customer controls budgets, timing and contract terms.
- Procurement is shifting towards other transaction authority awards and non-traditional rivals such as Anduril. Leidos' moat is narrow: incumbency, not pricing power.
- Group margin is about 12%, and three of four segments earn 7-10%.

KEY RISK: HEALTH
- It earns 46% of segment profit. Q3 profit fell 26%, and Q4 margin is guided to the high teens, down from 23%+.
- The VA recompete decision is expected April-May 2027. Health backlog is down 21%. 2027 is "not a bottom-line growth year".

CHECK BEFORE RELYING ON THE BEAR CASE
- The bear case may be too generous. It is 0% growth from an anchor that still includes pre-reset Health profit. The audit flagged this as an open, material issue.
- A rough stress test (my own arithmetic, not the pipeline): if Health stays at a high-teens margin on about $4.3bn of revenue, its operating profit is about $0.45bn lower than the FY25 run-rate. That is roughly a quarter off OE after tax, which would put the bear value near $115. So $115-120 may be the stressed-bear price, not a discount to it. Needs checking properly.
- The buy-below maths does not tie. The pipeline says 30% off bear ($152.5), which would be about $107, but it shows $118.9. Reconcile before quoting it.
- Entrust ($2.3bn) is valued at cost, with no earnings evidence.

CATALYSTS AND TRIGGERS
- The final VA request for proposals (due November).
- Q4 results (mid-to-late February): Health margin against "high teens".
- Full-year FY27 guidance, plus any continuing resolution or shutdown after the Democratic wins in Congress.
- Exit or trim: the VA recompete outcome is the main decision point. A loss of work share would break the thesis.

ENTRY PLAN
- Starter position at $115-120. Add only after the recompete clarity, not before.
- Size as a speculative or value-grade position (1-3% or 3-5% on the playbook), not a CORE holding.

EPD.text:
1. Stable toll like business with strong moat due to installed network 
2. Not affected by oil prices as it takes fee for using the pipelines
3. To enter at 31 or below. Strong cashflow business
4. Although key risk is that they are a debt funded business and interest rate likely will affect them and extremely capital intensive. But there is ability to pass on increased cost to customers
